signatures.claim: A reduction of the database connection pool size exhausted the pool under load
signatures.mechanism: With the pool reduced, concurrent requests exceed the available connections. Requests queue waiting for a connection, the wait exceeds the acquisition timeout, and the service returns 500s. Latency rises before errors appear because queueing precedes timing out.

requires.label: requests timed out acquiring a database connection
the pool size was changed shortly before onset
requires.demand: configuration changes for the service in the 30 minutes before onset

discriminators.reason: pool saturation distinguishes an exhausted pool from a database that is simply slow or unreachable

remediation.title: Restore the database connection pool size
remediation.rationale: Restoring the previous pool size removes the queueing that produces the timeouts, and is reversible in one step.
preconditions: the change that reduced the pool is confirmed by change evidence

signatures.claim: A traffic increase exceeded the service's capacity
signatures.mechanism: Request rate rose beyond what the current instance count can serve, so queueing raises latency and requests begin to fail. This explanation predicts that the same load has not been served successfully before.

discriminators.descriptor: historical peak traffic comparison at equal load
discriminators.reason: if an equal or greater load was served without error previously, load alone does not explain the failure

remediation.title: Reduce load on the service
remediation.rationale: Rate limiting sheds load while capacity is added, and is reversible.
preconditions: the traffic increase is confirmed to be organic

signatures.mechanism: If the database is down or unreachable, every query fails and connection errors dominate the logs. This explanation predicts that the database availability signal has dropped.

requires.label: database connection errors in the logs

discriminators.reason: an available database rules out an outage and leaves the connection errors to be explained another way

signatures.claim: A dependency endpoint was pointed at an unreachable host
signatures.mechanism: A configuration change replaced a dependency URL. Every call to that dependency fails to connect, so the calling service returns upstream errors while its own request rate is unchanged.

requires.label: a dependency URL was changed shortly before onset
requires.demand: configuration changes for the service in the 30 minutes before onset

discriminators.reason: upstream connect errors separate a dependency misconfiguration from a fault inside this service

remediation.title: Restore the dependency endpoint
remediation.rationale: Restoring the previous endpoint reverses the change that produced the connection failures.
preconditions: the previous endpoint is confirmed healthy

signatures.claim: A release introduced a query that does not use an index
signatures.mechanism: The new query performs a sequential scan, so each request holds the database longer. Database CPU rises and latency rises together while the error rate stays low, because requests are slow rather than failing.

requires.label: a release shortly before onset
requires.demand: configuration changes for the service in the 30 minutes before onset

discriminators.reason: database CPU rising with latency separates an inefficient query from a network or capacity problem

remediation.title: Enable safe mode to bypass the new query path
remediation.rationale: Safe mode routes around the new query while an index is prepared, and is reversible by flag.
preconditions: safe mode is known to serve the affected endpoint
